terra.problem: Saying the plan runs straight from Jerusalem to Rome adds a direct route that Paul does not specify.
Saying Paul stays to hold down the home base supplies a reason the text does not give.
The trip is presented as certain to come, but this passage only gives Paul's plans.
An ongoing operation with orders that keep coming in is more than the text says about the business.
The text says the shrines bring much business, not that the craftsmen have orders to fill.
The statement about Silas traveling with Paul elsewhere needs a reference.
The explanation is generic and ends by simply repeating that Demetrius means Paul.
The text does not place the meeting in a room or say everyone there is a silversmith. Workmen in related trades are also present.
Saying nobody locks up or heads home asserts details the passage does not give.
Timothy and Erastus were sent to Macedonia, but the passage does not explicitly establish that they are absent from the theatre.
Saying he would have helped hold the door places Papa Dorin in the Bible event, even hypothetically.
The text does not say the crowd showed up before anyone could explain why.
Most did not know why they were there. That does not mean the whole theatre had no clear reason for being there.
The explanation is flat and largely repeats the same hand-signal detail.
The passage does not say Alexander never got to make his defense.
The passage records the shouting but does not say Alexander never got a chance to finish his defense.
The clerk quiets the crowd before he speaks. Saying his speech starts by agreeing with them and that it works changes the sequence.
The text does not say the courts are quieter than the theatre.
The text calls for a legal assembly but does not say it must be open rather than hidden.
The explanation is generic and repeats the answer without adding a distinctive observation.
The clerk quiets the crowd before his speech and then dismisses the assembly. Saying the speech ended the whole thing goes beyond the text.
The disciples would not allow Paul to go before the assembly. His official friends begged him not to enter the theatre; the text does not say they kept him out.
